title: Riverside Public Utilities Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps, Batteries, EV Chargers
desc: What Riverside Public Utilities pays in 2026: heat pump $750 per ton, battery $500 per kWh up to $10,000, EV charger up to $1,500, insulation and windows. Riverside is not SCE.
lead: Riverside runs its own utility, so Southern California Edison guides do not apply here. Riverside Public Utilities pays $750 per ton for a heat pump, $500 per kWh for a battery and up to $1,500 for an EV charger. An older $3,100 figure on this site was wrong.
cards_intro: RPU's rebates are for residential electric customers and depend on available funds. We read its pages on October 2, 2026. Each card names the fact with the date and a source link.

cards.title: Heat pump and air conditioning
cards.amount: $750 per ton for a heat pump
cards.note: Heat pump 15.2 SEER or better. Central air conditioner $150 or $250 per ton, tune-up $25, Wi-Fi thermostat $50, whole-house evaporative cooler $150. Matching condenser and coil. Apply within 90 days.

cards.title: ENERGY STAR products
cards.note: Heat pump water heater $200, heat pump dryer $200, refrigerator with recycling $200, dishwasher $50, washer $75. Apply within 90 days.

cards.title: Weatherization
cards.amount: Insulation per sq ft; windows $1 per sq ft
cards.note: Attic insulation 10 to 20 cents per sq ft, walls 15 cents, ENERGY STAR windows and glass doors $1 per sq ft, plus duct, fan and cool roof lines.

cards.title: Energy storage
cards.note: $850 per kWh up to $17,000 for qualified low-income share customers. Purchases since July 1, 2026, on a time-of-use rate. Apply within 180 days.

cards.title: EV rebates
cards.note: $2,500 for share customers. Used EV up to $1,000, or $4,000 for share customers.

sections: Riverside is served by Riverside Public Utilities, not Southern California Edison. A guide that says otherwise is out of date. Check the name on your electric bill first, since a city address does not tell you which utility serves it. Moreno Valley is next door but has its own utility for part of the city, and its page shows how little is published there.

RPU wants a dated receipt that shows the make, model, serial number, tonnage and SEER of heat pump equipment, and it requires a matching condenser and coil. Most items need an application within 90 days of purchase, and storage within 180 days. Funds are limited. The battery rebate needs a domestic time-of-use rate, so check that the rate suits your household before you buy storage.

A 3-ton heat pump earns 3 x $750 = $2,250. A heat pump water heater adds $200, and 1,500 square feet of R-30 attic insulation at 15 cents adds $225. Together that is $2,675, before any battery or EV charger rebate. A 10 kWh battery at $500 per kWh would add $5,000.

RPU pays no rebate for rooftop solar panels on the pages we read. State and federal money is mostly out in 2026.

State and federal money adds little in 2026. TECH Clean California lists its single-family funds as reserved, the federal home electrification rebates are on hold, and the federal 25C and 25D credits ended after December 31, 2025.
claim_heading: How to claim an RPU rebate
claim_steps: Confirm your electric bill says Riverside Public Utilities.
Check the item on RPU's rebate page before you buy.
Keep the dated receipt with make, model, serial number and tonnage or size.
Apply within 90 days of purchase, or within 180 days for storage.
For storage, confirm you are on a domestic time-of-use rate first.

faq: No. Riverside runs Riverside Public Utilities.
How much does RPU pay for a heat pump?
$750 per ton for a heat pump of 15.2 SEER or better.
How much is the battery rebate?
$500 per kWh up to $10,000 for purchases since July 1, 2026, or $850 per kWh up to $17,000 for qualified low-income share customers.
Do I need a time-of-use rate for the battery rebate?
Yes. The applicant must be on a domestic time-of-use rate.
How long do I have to apply?
90 days from purchase for most items and 180 days for storage.
